title: Rita Levi-Montalcini (1909–2012) — The Turin Bedroom Lab, the Rio Mice, Snake Venom NGF, and the 103-Year Senator

teenKit.tldr: Rita Levi-Montalcini defied fascist laws, wartime devastation, and traditional gender roles by building a laboratory in her own bedroom, eventually smuggling live cancer tissues across continents to discover how nerves grow.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Her discovery of nerve growth factors unlocked our modern understanding of how brains wire themselves, laying the groundwork for treating neurodegenerative diseases and injuries.
keyTakeaways: Asymmetric improvisation means finding a way to do high-level work with minimal resources when official doors are locked.
Serendipity is useless without rigorous controls to spot and verify unexpected biological clues.
Composure under provocation allows sharp minds to outmaneuver systemic oppression and institutional gatekeeping.
